title: Psalms Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 17.

questions.question: What does David ask the LORD to hear in Psalms 17:1?
questions.explanation: David asks the LORD to attend unto his cry and give ear unto his prayer in Psalms 17:1.

questions.question: In Psalms 17:2, what does David request from the LORD?
questions.explanation: David requests that his sentence come forth from the LORD's presence in Psalms 17:2.

questions.question: What has the LORD done to David's heart according to Psalms 17:3?
questions.explanation: David states that the LORD has proved his heart in Psalms 17:3.

questions.question: According to Psalms 17:4, what has David kept himself from?
questions.explanation: David mentions that by the word of God's lips, he has kept himself from the paths of the destroyer in Psalms 17:4.

questions.question: In Psalms 17:5, what does David ask the LORD to do?
questions.explanation: David requests that the LORD hold up his goings in His paths in Psalms 17:5.

questions.question: True or False: David's prayer in Psalms 17 begins with a request for the LORD to hear him.
questions.explanation: In Psalms 17:1, David indeed requests the LORD to hear his prayer, making the statement true.

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 17:3, David claims that his mouth will not transgress.
questions.explanation: David expresses his determination that his mouth shall not transgress in Psalms 17:3, affirming the statement as true.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 17:4 indicates that David has not kept himself from any paths.
questions.explanation: In Psalms 17:4, David specifically states that he has kept himself from the paths of the destroyer, making the statement false.

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 17:2, David asks for the LORD to behold things that are unequal.
questions.explanation: David requests that the LORD behold things that are equal, not unequal, in Psalms 17:2, making the statement false.

questions.question: In what order does David request for the LORD to hold up his goings?
questions.explanation: David's request in Psalms 17:5 comes after he speaks about the LORD proving his heart in Psalms 17:3.

questions.question: What does David refer to himself as in Psalms 17:8?
questions.explanation: David asks the LORD to keep him as the apple of the eye in Psalms 17:8.

questions.question: What does David ask the LORD to show him in Psalms 17:7?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 17:7, David requests the LORD to show His marvellous lovingkindness.

questions.question: How does David describe the wicked in Psalms 17:10?
questions.explanation: David states that the wicked speak proudly in Psalms 17:10.

questions.question: What animal does David compare the wicked to in Psalms 17:12?
questions.explanation: David compares the wicked to a lion that is greedy of his prey in Psalms 17:12.

questions.question: What is David's hope in the end according to Psalms 17:15?
questions.explanation: David expresses that he will behold God's face in righteousness in Psalms 17:15.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 17:6, why does David call upon God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:6 explicitly states David called upon God because he believes God will hear him, and he asks God to incline His ear to hear his speech.

questions.question: How does Psalms 17:7 describe God's help for those who trust in Him?
options: He saves them by His right hand from their enemies
He gives them wealth and honor
He allows them to conquer kingdoms
He makes them rulers over others
questions.correctAnswer: He saves them by His right hand from their enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:7 says God saves those who trust in Him by His right hand from those who rise up against them, showing divine protection.

questions.question: What metaphor does David use in Psalms 17:8 to express how God should protect him?
options: Keep me as the apple of the eye and hide me under the shadow of thy wings
questions.correctAnswer: Keep me as the apple of the eye and hide me under the shadow of thy wings
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:8 uses the metaphor of God keeping David as the apple of the eye and hiding him under His wings, symbolizing close and tender protection.

questions.question: What type of enemies does David ask God to protect him from in Psalms 17:9?
options: The wicked who oppress and deadly enemies who compass him about
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked who oppress and deadly enemies who compass him about
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:9 specifically requests protection from wicked oppressors and deadly enemies who encircle him.

questions.question: In Psalms 17:10, how are David's enemies described in terms of their behavior and attitude?
options: Enclosed in their own fat and speaking proudly with their mouth
questions.correctAnswer: Enclosed in their own fat and speaking proudly with their mouth
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:10 describes the enemies as being self-indulgent ('enclosed in their own fat') and prideful in speech.

questions.question: What does Psalms 17:7 teach us about the relationship between trust in God and His protection?
options: God saves those who put their trust in Him from their adversaries
Trusting God leads to material wealth
God ignores those who trust Him
questions.correctAnswer: God saves those who put their trust in Him from their adversaries
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:7 reveals that God's marvellous lovingkindness particularly saves and protects those who place their trust in Him from their enemies.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 17:6 and 17:8, what combination of actions and promises highlight David's confidence in God's protection?
options: David calls upon God who listens, and God keeps him as the apple of the eye
David fights his enemies alone, and God rewards him
David hides and God remains silent
David ignores prayer and trusts his own strength
questions.correctAnswer: David calls upon God who listens, and God keeps him as the apple of the eye
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:6 shows David calling on God who hears him, and Psalms 17:8 depicts God's personal protection by keeping him as the apple of the eye.

questions.question: What does Psalms 17:9 imply about the nature of the threats David faces?
options: His enemies are aggressive and surround him closely
His enemies are indifferent and distant
His enemies are forgiving and kind
His enemies are weak and insignificant
questions.correctAnswer: His enemies are aggressive and surround him closely
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:9 speaks of enemies who oppress and deadly ones who compass him about, implying close, aggressive threats.

questions.question: According to Psalms 17:10, what is a characteristic of the wicked that oppress David, and why is this significant for Christian living?
options: They are proud in speech and self-indulgent, teaching us humility and vigilance
They are silent and humble, showing peacefulness
They are generous and kind, modeling charity
questions.correctAnswer: They are proud in speech and self-indulgent, teaching us humility and vigilance
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:10 describes the wicked as proud and self-indulgent, highlighting the need for humility and alertness against such attitudes.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 17:6 teaches that God will not hear the prayers of the faithful.
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:6 clearly states that God hears the prayers of the faithful, as David calls upon God who inclines His ear to listen.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 17:8 uses the imagery of God’s wings to illustrate protection and care.
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:8 uses the metaphor of being hidden under the shadow of God's wings to illustrate His protective care, similar to a bird protecting its young.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 17:9 indicates that David’s enemies are distant and not a serious threat.
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:9 says David’s enemies compass him about and oppress him, showing they are close and dangerous.

questions.question: What lesson about prayer and trust can a believer learn from the connection between Psalms 17:6 and 17:7?
options: Calling on God leads to His hearing and marvelous saving kindness for those who trust Him
Prayer is only effective if accompanied by sacrifices
God favors only the strongest believers
Trusting God removes all troubles immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Calling on God leads to His hearing and marvelous saving kindness for those who trust Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:6 shows God hears when called upon, and Psalms 17:7 reveals God’s saving kindness for those who trust Him, teaching believers to pray with trust.

questions.question: How does Psalms 17:10 and 17:11 together describe the manner in which David's enemies pursue him?
options: They are proud and surround him stealthily with their eyes cast down
They ignore him and keep distance
questions.correctAnswer: They are proud and surround him stealthily with their eyes cast down
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:10 describes them as proud in speech, and 17:11 says they compass his steps with eyes bowing to the earth, indicating stealth and pride.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue is emphasized by David’s request in Psalms 17:8 to be kept as the 'apple of the eye' and hidden under God's wings?
questions.explanation: David's request in Psalms 17:8 illustrates a trustful faith in God's close and personal protection, a key virtue in Christian living.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 17.

questions.question: What imagery is used in Psalms 17:12 to describe the enemies surrounding the psalmist?
options: Like a lion greedy for his prey and a young lion lurking in secret places
questions.correctAnswer: Like a lion greedy for his prey and a young lion lurking in secret places
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:12 uses the imagery of a lion greedy for prey and a young lion lurking in secret places to depict the enemies as dangerous and stealthy predators.

questions.question: According to Psalms 17:15, what will satisfy the psalmist when he awakes?
options: Beholding God's face in righteousness and His likeness
questions.correctAnswer: Beholding God's face in righteousness and His likeness
questions.explanation: Verse 15 expresses the psalmist's hope and satisfaction in beholding God's face in righteousness and being satisfied with His likeness upon awakening.

questions.question: In Psalms 17:14, what is said about the portion of men of the world?
options: They have no portion in this life
They have their portion in this life and fill their belly with hidden treasure
questions.correctAnswer: They have their portion in this life and fill their belly with hidden treasure
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:14 states that men of the world have their portion in this life and that God fills their belly with hidden treasure, indicating their focus on worldly gain.

questions.question: What request does the psalmist make to the LORD in Psalms 17:13?
options: To grant him riches and honor
To arise, disappoint the enemy, cast him down, and deliver his soul from the wicked
To send a messenger to his enemies
To grant him long life and peace
questions.correctAnswer: To arise, disappoint the enemy, cast him down, and deliver his soul from the wicked
questions.explanation: In Psalms 17:13, the psalmist asks the LORD to arise and defeat his enemies, delivering him from the wicked who are God's instruments.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 17:14 where the wicked are described as 'full of children' and leaving their substance to their babes?
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:14 employs parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device, by repeating and balancing ideas about the wicked being full of children and leaving their substance to their offspring.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'apple of the eye' in Psalms 17:8 symbolize?
questions.explanation: 'Apple of the eye' in Psalms 17:8 signifies someone cherished and carefully protected, highlighting the psalmist's plea for God's safeguarding.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 17:11, the enemies have set their eyes to the heavens in defiance.
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:11 says the enemies have set their eyes bowing down to the earth, not to the heavens, indicating a posture of stealth or submission.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of divine protection seen in Psalms 17:8 about being 'hidden under the shadow of thy wings'?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:11 uses the imagery of an eagle hovering and protecting its young, similar to the 'shadow of thy wings' in Psalms 17:8, symbolizing God's care and protection.

questions.question: How does Psalms 17:3 demonstrate the psalmist's confidence in his integrity before God?
options: By claiming he has many enemies
By declaring he is purposed that his mouth shall not transgress and will be found blameless after testing
questions.correctAnswer: By declaring he is purposed that his mouth shall not transgress and will be found blameless after testing
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:3 shows the psalmist's confidence as God has tested his heart and found no fault, and he intends not to sin with his speech.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the hope expressed in Psalms 17:15 about beholding God's likeness upon awakening?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:12 speaks of seeing 'face to face' and knowing fully, paralleling Psalms 17:15's hope to behold God's face and be satisfied with His likeness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 17:10, what characterizes the wicked who oppress the psalmist?
options: They are enclosed in their own fat and speak proudly with their mouth
questions.correctAnswer: They are enclosed in their own fat and speak proudly with their mouth
questions.explanation: Verse 10 describes the wicked as self-indulgent ('enclosed in their own fat') and arrogant, boasting with their mouths.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 17:6 highlights the psalmist's assurance that God will hear his call.
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:6 expresses confidence that God will hear the psalmist's call and incline His ear to listen to his speech.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'sentence' in Psalms 17:2 likely mean in this context?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 17:2, 'sentence' refers to a judgment or verdict from God's presence, asking for divine justice based on equality and fairness.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the enemies’ strategy as depicted in Psalms 17:11-12?
options: They surround the psalmist stealthily, like lions ready to pounce
questions.correctAnswer: They surround the psalmist stealthily, like lions ready to pounce
questions.explanation: Verses 11-12 depict enemies as surrounding the psalmist with eyes downcast and likened to lions lying in wait, indicating stealth and predatory intent.

questions.question: How does Psalms 17:7 express the relationship between trust in God and salvation?
options: Those who trust in God are saved by His right hand from their enemies
Trust is only for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Those who trust in God are saved by His right hand from their enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:7 promises that God saves those who put their trust in Him by His powerful right hand from adversaries.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does David request from the Lord in Psalms 17:1?
questions.explanation: David prays for the Lord to hear his right, indicating his plea for justice and attention to his honest cry (Psalms 17:1). This reflects the theme of seeking divine justice.

questions.question: According to Psalms 17:3, how does David feel about his own heart?
questions.explanation: David states that after being tested by God, He will find nothing in his heart, indicating his commitment to purity and integrity (Psalms 17:3).

questions.question: What does David ask the Lord to do in Psalms 17:5?
options: Hold up his goings in God's paths
questions.correctAnswer: Hold up his goings in God's paths
questions.explanation: David seeks divine guidance and support to prevent his steps from slipping, emphasizing reliance on God's direction (Psalms 17:5).

questions.question: In Psalms 17:7, what does David refer to when he mentions 'marvellous lovingkindness'?
questions.explanation: David appeals to God's lovingkindness, which reflects His mercy and compassion towards those who trust in Him (Psalms 17:7).

questions.question: What imagery does David use to describe his desire for protection in Psalms 17:8?
options: As the apple of the eye
questions.correctAnswer: As the apple of the eye
questions.explanation: David uses the phrase 'apple of the eye' to express his desire for God to protect him with utmost care (Psalms 17:8).

questions.question: What do the 'wicked' do to David according to Psalms 17:9?
questions.explanation: David describes his plight, stating that he is oppressed by the wicked, who surround him as deadly enemies (Psalms 17:9).

questions.question: According to Psalms 17:10, what do the wicked do in their pride?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that the wicked are arrogant, speaking proudly, which highlights their rebellion against God (Psalms 17:10).

questions.question: What metaphor does David use for the wicked in Psalms 17:12?
options: As a wolf in sheep's clothing
As a lion greedy of prey
questions.correctAnswer: As a lion greedy of prey
questions.explanation: David likens the wicked to a lion, illustrating their predatory nature and their intent to harm (Psalms 17:12).

questions.question: What does David ask the Lord to do regarding the wicked in Psalms 17:13?
questions.explanation: David requests deliverance from the wicked, indicating his reliance on God as the ultimate defender (Psalms 17:13).

questions.question: In Psalms 17:14, what is the fate of the wicked according to David's observations?
options: They will leave their substance to their babes
questions.correctAnswer: They will leave their substance to their babes
questions.explanation: David notes that the wicked, despite their earthly success, ultimately leave their wealth to their children, highlighting the temporal nature of their prosperity (Psalms 17:14).

questions.question: What does David express he will do in Psalms 17:15?
questions.explanation: David expresses confidence that he will see God in righteousness, indicating hope in divine fellowship and future restoration (Psalms 17:15).

questions.question: What does Psalms 17:2 teach about divine justice?
options: It is based on human standards
questions.explanation: David asks for his sentence to come from God's presence, indicating belief in God's fair and equal judgment (Psalms 17:2).

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be drawn from Psalms 17:4 and Psalms 17:3 regarding human integrity?
questions.explanation: David acknowledges that God has probed his heart and found it without transgression, indicating that integrity is subject to divine scrutiny (Psalms 17:3-4).

questions.question: How do Psalms 17:5 and Psalms 17:11 together convey a message about divine guidance?
options: God supports the righteous in their journey
Guidance is only for the wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: God supports the righteous in their journey
questions.explanation: David's plea for God to hold up his steps and the mention of the wicked compassing him convey that God’s guidance is crucial amidst opposition (Psalms 17:5, 11).

questions.question: What is the apologetic insight regarding the prosperity of the wicked as seen in Psalms 17:14?
options: Sceptics claim the wicked prosper without consequence. What does Psalms 17:14 teach?
The wicked will be punished immediately
Earthly success does not equate to divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: Earthly success does not equate to divine favor
questions.explanation: Psalms 17:14 shows that while the wicked may prosper in this life, their ultimate fate is separate from divine approval, underscoring the transient nature of worldly success.
